about: Totals of years before the first king, as two texts give them. Figures are what the text says, cited to its line or fragment and page, never measurements; plus_x marks a damaged total read as a minimum. Unchecked against the editions themselves (Gardiner 1959, Ryholt 2004, Waddell 1940's pages) until someone reads them.

figures.text: The Turin King List (Royal Canon of Turin)
figures.locus: column II, line 8 (Gardiner); row 3.8 at pharaoh.se
figures.reading: ... of the spirits and the followers of Horus, 13420 (+ x) years
figures.note: The site gives no uncertainty note for this numeral beyond the + x. The script's 'in the most probable reading of its damaged numbers' covers this line and the next.

figures.text: The Turin King List (Royal Canon of Turin)
figures.locus: column II, line 9 (Gardiner); row 3.9 at pharaoh.se
figures.reading: their lifetime to the followers of Horus: 23200 (+ x) years
figures.note: The site: the year-sign traces are clear and the two ten-thousand signs very probable. Whether this total includes line 8's or runs before it is open (docs/script.md, open questions); adding the two is Schwaller de Lubicz's reading, not a figure on the papyrus.

figures.reading: is reckoned to have comprised in all 24,900 lunar years, which make 2206 solar years
figures.note: The gods, demigods and spirits before the first dynasty, all told. Read on LacusCurtius's transcription of Waddell, page marker p. 7.

figures.reading: 24,900 lunar years, which make 2206 solar years
figures.note: Eusebius's own conversion, in the text, not ours. Waddell's note 8: Boeckh corrects 2206 to 2046.
